IncidentBot: ALERT: production /v1/generate p95 > 800ms (rule: gen-api-p95). paging oncall @alexk (pager duty).
Alex K: on it. seeing p50=90ms p95=980ms p99=1.4s on gen-cluster-1. error rate for streaming endpoints up ~3%.
Alex K: first quick question — do we have a recent config that increased batch window?
Kevin L: not recently, but we've had a sudden spike in long sequences; continuous batching might be starving small requests.
Kevin L: idea: increase continuous_batch.window_ms from 20 -> 100 for prod-gen-1 to reduce kernel churn. will trade a bit of median latency for much higher throughput.
Sophie R: agree. also we can apply temporary ingress rate limits for non-SLA orgs, plus lower free-tier quotas to take the easiest load off.
Alex K: risks? any customers dependent on sub-100ms interactive latency that would break?
Kevin L: a few RTA customers might see worse interactive feel, but they have SLOs and we can pin them to low-latency path in routing. non-critical customers will be throttled.
Alex K: ok let's do two-phase: 1) apply batching window bump on gen-cluster-1; 2) enable ingress shaping for free-tier; 3) disable reranking for heavy tenants as fallback.
Alex K: running change now via admin API: ```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/clusters/prod-gen-1/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"continuous_batch.window_ms":100}'
```
DeployBot: CONFIG APPLIED: continuous_batch.window_ms=100 -> prod-gen-1 (applied by alexk). rolling update started; 6/12 hosts updated.
Alex K: also applying temporary rate limit rule for free-tier: global_rps_limit.free=400. command: ```
rbacctl set-rate-limit --policy free-tier --rps 400 --duration 30m
```
DeployBot: RATE LIMIT RULE APPLIED: free-tier rps=400 (expires in 30m)
Maria T: taking over handoff at 04:20 UTC. watching logs and SLO dashboards.
Maria T: metrics after batch window change: p95 dropped from 980ms -> 420ms over 2m, errors down from 3.2% -> 0.9%. p50 up a hair 90ms -> 130ms.
Kevin L: good. we should still disable noncritical rerankers for three heavy orgs: org-17, org-42, org-88. command: ```
admin feature-flag set --org org-17 rerank.enabled false
admin feature-flag set --org org-42 rerank.enabled false
admin feature-flag set --org org-88 rerank.enabled false
```
Alex K: done, flags flipped. customers notified via CS for org-42 and org-88 since they are paying.
IncidentBot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: 12 orgs had >5% transient errors during spike, 3 orgs experienced request timeouts. CS ticket created: INC-2026-473.
Maria T: summary for handoff: current state = stabilizing. mitigations applied = batching window increase, free-tier rate limit, rerank disabled for heavy tenants, quota override for one noisy org (org-99 lowered to 10k tokens/day). observability = dashboards show p95 improvement, watchlist created.
Sophie R: can we consider a short-term quota override script to auto-detect noisy orgs and throttle? I can draft it.
Kevin L: long-term action: dynamic batching based on live seq-length histograms, and a safer fast rollback for continuous_batch changes. follow-up action item on the postmortem.
Alex K: agreed. I'll keep watch for 30m and then we can relax rate limits if stable. handoff notes: Maria, if p95 creeps back above 700ms, revert window to 20ms and trigger capacity scale (scale-up-gpu pool).
Maria T: noted. I'll also add a quick note to the oncall runbook about tradeoffs of continuous_batch changes — make explicit customer-impact zones.
Sophie R: :thumbsup:
Alex K: closing pager for now. will open incident bridge + postmortem doc once stabilized. thanks everyone for fast coord.
DeployBot: ROLLING UPDATE: prod-gen-1 hosts updated 12/12. no failed hosts.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT status: mitigated -> monitoring. postmortem owner: alexk.
Maria T: moving to watch mode, will update thread if anything regresses.
